record.original_question: Does the collection of known polynomial invariants of degree at most 9 cut out the algebraic variety of 4×4×4 contingency tables (pijk) over C that have tensor rank at most 4, equivalently tables admitting a decomposition pijk = ρAi·σAj·θAk + ρCi·σCj·θCk + ρGi·σGj·θGk + ρTi·σTj·θTk for i, j, k ∈ {A, C, G, T}?

evidence.quote: Specific Problem: Consider the variety of 4×4×4-tables of tensor rank at most 4. There are certain known polynomials of degree at most nine which vanish on this variety. Do they suffice to cut out the variety?

The model referred to in the Specific Problem lives in the 64-dimensional space C^4 ⊗ C^4 ⊗ C^4 of 4×4×4-tables (pijk), where i, j, k ∈ {A, C, G, T}. It has the parametric representation pijk = ρAi · σAj · θAk + ρCi · σCj · θCk + ρGi · σGj · θGk + ρTi · σTj · θTk.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the 64-dimensional complex vector space $V = \mathbb{C}^4 \otimes \mathbb{C}^4 \otimes \mathbb{C}^4$ of $4\times 4\times 4$ tensors $(p_{ijk})_{i,j,k \in \{A,C,G,T\}}$. Let $X \subseteq V$ denote the (Zariski closure of the) set of tensors of tensor rank at most $4$, i.e. tensors admitting a decomposition
$$p_{ijk} = \rho^A_i \sigma^A_j \theta^A_k + \rho^C_i \sigma^C_j \theta^C_k + \rho^G_i \sigma^G_j \theta^G_k + \rho^T_i \sigma^T_j \theta^T_k$$
for some vectors $\rho^a, \sigma^a, \theta^a \in \mathbb{C}^4$ ($a \in \{A,C,G,T\}$). Among the polynomials known to vanish identically on $X$ are: (i) the Strassen commutation relations of degree $5$; (ii) the Landsberg–Manivel polynomials of degree $6$; and (iii) certain symmetrization-type polynomials of degree $9$. Let $J$ be the ideal generated by all such known invariants of degree at most $9$. Question: does the zero locus $V(J) \subseteq V$ coincide set-theoretically with $X$?
artifact.status_search_result: The set-theoretic Salmon conjecture for the variety of 4×4×4 complex tensors of border rank at most 4 has been proved. Friedland and Gross gave a proof (arXiv:1104.1776, J. Algebra 2012) showing this variety is cut out by polynomials of degrees 5, 6, and 9 (Strassen, Landsberg–Manivel, and symmetrization equations). A complementary computational proof appears in Bates–Oeding, "Toward a Salmon Conjecture" (Experimental Mathematics, 2011). The ideal-theoretic version (full generators of the prime ideal) remained more delicate, but the set-theoretic question posed here is resolved affirmatively.

status_evidence.title: A proof of the set-theoretic version of the salmon conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: We prove that the variety of 4×4×4 complex valued tensors of border rank at most 4 is the zero set of polynomial equations of degree 5, 6, and 9.
status_evidence.claim: Set-theoretic Salmon conjecture proved by Friedland–Gross.

status_evidence.title: Toward a Salmon Conjecture (Bates–Oeding)
status_evidence.snippet: Numerical algebraic geometry combined with representation theory shows the variety is cut out by the known polynomials of degrees 6 and 9, together with Landsberg–Manivel.
status_evidence.claim: Computational solution of the set-theoretic Salmon problem.
